name: Lindworm
description: A lindworm is a serpentine dragon of Germanic, Norse and Central European folklore — typically wingless, with two clawed forelimbs in continental traditions and entirely limbless in much Swedish lore. Unlike fire-breathing medieval dragons, lindworms emphasise venom, constriction, and treasure-hoarding.

aliases.name: Hjulorm
aliases.meaning: 'wheel-worm' — variant that bites its tail to roll

origin: Lindworm folklore is concentrated in the Germanic-speaking and North European world: Scandinavia, the German-speaking lands, the Low Countries, and the British Isles, with regional offshoots reaching into Slavic and Baltic dragon imagery.
